source_text: Tamen cum hoc ibi satiatissime constet effectum, breviter licet, in praesenti quoque disputatione repetetur. Convertamur ergo ad ipsum, cuius cum eruditione decertamus. Annuis nempe, a nobis recte fuisse collectum, quia si fetus non nisi per sexum, si sexus non nisi per corpus, si corpus non nisi per Deum exstitisset, ambigi non posset fecunditatem ad Dei opera pertinere, nihilque suum in sexibus agnoscere principem tenebrarum, propter quod fructus eorum iuris sui assertione retineret; quia et diversitas pertinebat ad sexum, et commixtio ad membrorum diversitatem, et fructus fecunditatis ad Deum, qui etiam generantium fuerat institutor; ac per hoc nihil remanserat propter quod diabolo esset commixtionis adiudicanda fertilitas. Quod ergo tibi putas vel solatium vel praesidium a sermonis mei honestate conferri, quia nolui in hoc loco carnis concupiscentiam nominare? Quod etsi in omni opere silentio praeterissem, nihil tamen vituperationis aut iniuriae res illa susciperet, quae honestioribus signata nominibus vindicabatur, et clarissimis quidem intellegentiae vocibus. Fac igitur me prudentius, quam suscepti negotii ratio petebat, tegere voluisse silentio nomen eius rei, quam tegimus amictu; num ideo totius rationis, totius veritatis iactura facienda est? Num ideo negotiorum arbiter intellectus iacebit, quia est aliquid, quod ut ante oculos, ita ad aures non semper decore possit adduci? Verumtamen quid deformitatis habet, carnis concupiscentiam nominare; quam et ego appellavi, cum poposcit locus; et tu licet indomabilem te eam sentire confirmes, tamen crebro commemoras?
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless, although this stands as having been accomplished there most fully, it will be repeated, though briefly, in the present disputation also. Let us turn therefore to him himself, with whose learning we contend. You grant, surely, that it was rightly gathered by us that if the offspring had not existed except through sex, if sex not except through a body, if a body not except through God, it could not be doubted that fertility belongs to God's works, and that the prince of darkness recognizes nothing of his own in the sexes on account of which he would retain their fruit by assertion of his own right; because both difference belonged to sex, and mingling to the difference of members, and the fruit of fertility to God, who had been also the institutor of those generating; and through this nothing had remained on account of which the fertility of mingling should be adjudged to the devil. What therefore do you think is conferred on you as comfort or protection from the decency of my speech, because I was unwilling in this place to name the desire of the flesh? Which even if I had passed over in silence in the whole work, nevertheless that matter would receive no blame or injury, which was being claimed as marked by more honorable names, and indeed by the clearest voices of understanding. Suppose therefore that I wanted more cautiously than the reason of the undertaken business asked to cover by silence the name of that thing which we cover with a garment; must therefore the loss of all reason, of all truth, be made? Will the intellect, the arbiter of businesses, therefore lie prostrate, because there is something which, as before the eyes, so to the ears cannot always be brought becomingly? Yet what deformity does it have to name the desire of the flesh, which both I called when the place demanded, and you, although you confirm that you feel it untamable, nevertheless commemorate frequently?

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Although this was established there with the fullest possible treatment, it must also be repeated, briefly, in the present discussion. Let us turn, then, to the man himself, whose learning we are contesting. You agree, surely, that I reasoned correctly: if offspring exist only through sex, sex only through a body, and a body only through God, there can be no doubt that fertility belongs among God’s works. The ruler of darkness recognizes nothing of his own in the sexes by which he could keep their offspring as his rightful property. For their difference belonged to sex, their union to the difference of their organs, and the fruit of fertility to God, who had also established those who generate offspring. Accordingly, nothing remained for which the fertility of sexual union should be awarded to the devil.

What comfort or defense, then, do you think the decency of my language gives you because I did not wish to name the desire of the flesh in this passage? Even if I had passed it over in silence throughout the whole work, that would have brought no blame or injury upon the thing itself. It was being defended under more decent names, and indeed in language perfectly clear to the understanding. Suppose, then, that with more reserve than the subject required I had chosen to veil in silence the name of what we cover with clothing. Must all reason and all truth therefore be thrown away? Must understanding, the judge of matters, therefore lie helpless because there is something that cannot always be brought decently before the ears, just as it cannot always be brought before the eyes? Yet what is ugly about naming the desire of the flesh? I have named it when the occasion required, and you mention it frequently, although you insist that you find it untamable.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)
